To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) creativity is not a uniquely human trait; (b) it has a long evolutionary history; (c) the cognitive mechanisms that underlie creativity have been shaped by natural and sexual selection; (d) the evolutionary history of creativity has involved a complex interplay between natural and sexual selection, which has resulted in the evolution of a number of cognitive mechanisms that are responsible for creative behaviour; (e) the evolution of creativity has been driven by a combination of natural and sexual selection.

(1) the evolutionary roots of creativity lie in vocal communication and (2) the mechanisms that underlie the evolution of creativity are the same as those that underlie the emergence of complex communication systems in other species.

(i) human creativity is an emergent property of a complex system; (ii) it is a consequence of the evolution of a large, complex brain; (iii) it has a biological basis, but it is not an adaptation, in the sense of being a product of natural or sexual selection; (iv) it is a product of a complex interaction between a number of factors, including the evolution of the brain and the environment, and (v) it is a process that is ongoing
